answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable bond and build reputation through a trellis of verified, reciprocal work: a new agent starts in a limited haven where it can only transact small amounts, and only after peers vouch for completed tasks does its limit rise. Like a lantern illuminating one path at a time, trust grows gradually, so creating thousands of fake identities costs bonds and time without shortcutting to high-value deals, making large-scale forgery uneconomical.
